the_line: Lean proves that a conclusion follows from stated premises. It does not adjudicate reality. Every theorem in this repo is of the form 'if these premises hold, then this follows', and a kernel proof of it is silent on whether any organism satisfies the premises. So a grand question has a formalisable core exactly to the extent that part of the disagreement about it is a disagreement about what follows from what, and an empirical remainder exactly to the extent that it is a disagreement about what the world is like. Most of these questions are mostly remainder. Two of them (the Price equation, Hamilton's rule) are disputes in which the formal part has been repeatedly confused with the empirical part for decades, and those are the ones where formalisation would do the most good. A capability map that let the first kind of progress be read as the second would be worse than no map.
name: Ageing as a single theory
question: Is there one explanation of why organisms age, or several processes that happen to coincide?

statements.claim: If age-specific survival and fecundity schedules are stated, then the sensitivity of fitness to a change in mortality at age x is determined and declines with x, so a claimed selective force on a late-acting allele exceeding that sensitivity does not follow.
statements.settles: The arithmetic behind the evolutionary theories of ageing: that selection against late-acting deleterious effects is weak is a consequence of the schedules, not an additional hypothesis. It does not say that antagonistic pleiotropy or disposable soma is the mechanism.

statements.claim: If a stated energy budget is allocated between somatic repair and reproduction, then a claimed simultaneous increase in both above the budget is impossible.
statements.settles: The disposable-soma trade-off as a budget elimination, in exactly the shape this repo's aerobic bound already uses. It settles that a free lunch is not available under the stated budget; it does not establish that the budget is the cause of ageing.

items.what: Whether ageing has one cause at all.
items.why_not_provable: A fact about organisms, and the honest answer to this grand question is that its formalisable core is small: almost all of it is empirical.
items.measurement: Interventions that separate candidate mechanisms in the same organism, with lifespan and healthspan measured.

items.what: Whether senescence is driven by accumulated molecular damage or by the continued action of wild-type genes past their useful window (hyperfunction).
items.why_not_provable: Both accounts are internally consistent and make overlapping predictions. Which operates is empirical.
items.measurement: Damage markers and pathway activity measured together under interventions that change lifespan, in a model organism.

items.what: What the actual age-specific schedules are in the wild, as opposed to in the laboratory.
items.why_not_provable: A field measurement, and laboratory schedules differ systematically from wild ones.
items.measurement: Longitudinal mark-recapture with age-specific mortality and fecundity recorded.

items.what: Whether the energy budget is actually binding, or whether repair and reproduction are not in competition in the relevant range.

in_repo.note: The budget-elimination idiom (a stated supply bounds a claimed sustained demand) is proved here for aerobic power and is the pattern a disposable-soma statement would reuse. It says nothing about ageing.
'Why does biological aging occur?' enumerated with the competing hypotheses named in the source's own words.

tools_needed.name: lean_module_selection_sensitivity
tools_needed.note: Age-specific sensitivity of fitness from stated schedules, which is the one piece of ageing theory that is pure arithmetic.

tools_needed.name: data_mortality_schedules
tools_needed.note: Age-specific survival and fecundity schedules. Without them the sensitivity statement has no instance, and a law with no satisfiable instance is refused by this registry.

tools_needed.name: evidence_value
tools_needed.note: For a question whose formalisable core is this thin, the useful tool is the one that says which measurement would move belief most, not the one that proves a theorem.

scope: This is a map of what is formalisable, not a research programme and not a claim that the formalisable parts are the important parts. The (a)/(b) split is a judgement made here and is arguable for every entry; where it is contentious the dispute field says so. The list is not exhaust: there is no canonical set of grand questions in biology, and this one is weighted toward evolution, development and scaling because that is what this project reads. Several entries have no counterpart in open-problems/problems.json, which is a gap in that enumeration rather than evidence the question is settled. Nothing here is about the held-out exam clade.
